title: Growing Up, Bodies, Boundaries & Fairness

myths.myth: Periods are dirty or shameful.
myths.truth: Menstruation is a normal, healthy body process.
myths.explanation: Roughly half the world menstruates — it's nothing to hide.

myths.myth: Only girls' bodies change at puberty.
myths.truth: Everyone's body changes during puberty.
myths.explanation: Boys, girls and all kids grow and change, at their own pace.

myths.myth: Erections or wet dreams mean something's wrong.
myths.truth: They're a normal part of growing up.
myths.explanation: Bodies are just learning new things; it's expected.

myths.myth: You should already know all about puberty.
myths.truth: It's normal to have questions — ask a trusted adult or doctor.
myths.explanation: Everyone learns this; no question is silly.

myths.myth: Boys shouldn't hear about periods.
myths.truth: Everyone should understand menstruation.
myths.explanation: Understanding helps everyone be supportive, not awkward.

myths.myth: Stress or sadness means you're weak.
myths.truth: Everyone struggles sometimes — it's human.
myths.explanation: Strong people are the ones who reach out.

myths.myth: You should handle big feelings alone.
myths.truth: Talking to someone helps.
myths.explanation: A trusted adult, friend or counsellor can help you carry it.

myths.myth: Mental health isn't a real thing.
myths.truth: Your mind needs care, just like your body.
myths.explanation: Looking after your mind is health, not weakness.

myths.myth: Asking for help is embarrassing.
myths.truth: Asking for help is smart and brave.
myths.explanation: Everyone needs help sometimes — that's normal.

myths.myth: Babies are brought by storks or just 'found'.
myths.truth: A baby grows from an egg and a sperm, in a uterus.
myths.explanation: The real story is science — and nothing to be ashamed of.

myths.myth: Talking about reproduction is dirty.
myths.truth: It's how all living things make new life.
myths.explanation: Knowing the facts is healthy and normal.

myths.myth: Only girls need to learn about reproduction.
myths.truth: Everyone should understand how bodies work.
myths.explanation: It takes understanding from everyone.

myths.myth: You can 'catch' a baby like a cold.
myths.truth: Pregnancy happens in specific ways you'll learn about.
myths.explanation: Facts replace scary playground rumours.

myths.myth: If you said yes once, you can't say no later.
myths.truth: You can change your mind any time.
myths.explanation: Consent is ongoing — no means no, always.

myths.myth: Family and friends don't need to ask first.
myths.truth: Everyone should ask; you can say no.
myths.explanation: Your body, your boundaries — even with people you love.

myths.myth: Online friends are just like real friends.
myths.truth: People online aren't always who they say.
myths.explanation: Guard private info; tell a trusted adult if something feels off.

myths.myth: Being polite matters more than feeling safe.
myths.truth: You can say no and leave; then tell a trusted adult.
myths.explanation: Your safety comes before politeness, every time.

myths.myth: Keeping an adult's secret is being loyal.
myths.truth: Secrets that make you uncomfortable should be told.
myths.explanation: Safe adults don't ask kids to keep secrets.

myths.myth: Jealousy proves someone really cares.
myths.truth: Controlling or jealous behaviour isn't love.
myths.explanation: Healthy relationships are built on trust and respect.

myths.myth: Real friends never disagree.
myths.truth: Disagreeing and making up is normal.
myths.explanation: How you handle conflict matters more than avoiding it.

myths.myth: You should change yourself to fit in.
myths.truth: Good friends like the real you.
myths.explanation: Belonging shouldn't cost you who you are.

myths.myth: Peer pressure means you have to go along.
myths.truth: You can say no and still be liked.
myths.explanation: Real friends respect your choices.

myths.myth: Boys are naturally better at maths; girls at caring.
myths.truth: Skills aren't decided by gender.
myths.explanation: Stereotypes limit everyone's potential.

myths.myth: Leadership is a man's role.
myths.truth: Anyone can lead.
myths.explanation: Great leaders come in every gender.

myths.myth: Housework is women's responsibility.
myths.truth: Care work belongs to everyone.
myths.explanation: Sharing it fairly is what equality looks like.

myths.myth: 'That's just how things are.'
myths.truth: Norms can change — and they have.
myths.explanation: People rewrite unfair rules all the time.

myths.myth: Questioning traditions is disrespectful.
myths.truth: Asking 'is this fair?' is healthy.
myths.explanation: Respect and fairness can grow together.

myths.myth: One person can't change anything.
myths.truth: Change often starts with a single voice.
myths.explanation: Big movements begin with individuals.

myths.myth: Gender rules are the same everywhere and always.
myths.truth: They vary across time and place.
myths.explanation: That shows they're made by people — and can be remade.

myths.myth: Staying quiet keeps the peace.
myths.truth: Speaking up safely can stop harm.
myths.explanation: Silence can let unfairness carry on.

myths.myth: Reporting bullying is snitching.
myths.truth: Reporting harm is responsible, not snitching.
myths.explanation: It protects people who are being hurt.

myths.myth: If it's not physical, it isn't bullying.
myths.truth: Words and being left out can hurt too.
myths.explanation: Emotional harm is real harm.

myths.myth: Only 'dirty' people get sick.
myths.truth: Anyone can catch an illness.
myths.explanation: Germs don't judge; prevention helps everyone.

myths.myth: Vaccines aren't necessary.
myths.truth: Vaccines train your body to fight disease.
myths.explanation: They protect you and the people around you.

myths.myth: Being healthy is all about how you look.
myths.truth: Health is how your body and mind feel and work.
myths.explanation: Care beats appearance.

myths.myth: You can always tell if someone is sick.
myths.truth: Many illnesses aren't visible.
myths.explanation: That's exactly why kindness and care matter.
